elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement for convenience.
elements.evidence: Article IV.IV expressly permits Licensee to terminate for convenience, in whole or in part, at any time.

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice.
elements.evidence: Article IV.IV requires thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Licensor.

elements.element: Customer receives a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees for the period following the effective date of termination.
elements.evidence: Licensor must refund prepaid fees, including prepaid Technical Support Services fees, covering the period after the effective date of termination. This operates as a pro-rata refund of unused prepaid fees.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: Article IV.IV states that Licensor has no right to terminate for convenience during the Initial Period or any extension thereof.

elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement for convenience.
elements.evidence: Article IV.IV expressly grants Licensee a termination-for-convenience right.

elements.element: Customer termination for convenience requires between sixty (60) and ninety (90) days' notice.
elements.evidence: The clause requires only thirty (30) days' prior written notice, which is outside the required 60–90-day range.

elements.element: If an early-termination fee applies, it does not exceed three months' fees.
elements.evidence: The condition is demonstrably absent: Article IV.IV permits termination without penalty or early-termination charge, so the applicable fee is zero and does not exceed the cap.

elements.element: Vendor has a right to terminate for convenience at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: The clause does not affirmatively grant Licensor a termination-for-convenience right at the end of a term; it only prohibits such termination during the Initial Period or an extension.

elements.element: Vendor may not terminate for convenience before the end of a term.
elements.evidence: Licensor is expressly denied any termination-for-convenience right during the Initial Period or any extension.

elements.element: Any Vendor termination for convenience requires ninety (90) days' notice.
elements.evidence: The condition is demonstrably absent because the rendered language grants Licensor no termination-for-convenience right. Accordingly, there is no Vendor convenience termination to which a notice requirement could apply, although the separate requirement to grant an end-of-term right is not met.

result.reason: The operative language fully satisfies the preferred position. The fallback is not fully satisfied because the Customer notice period is 30 rather than 60–90 days and Vendor receives no affirmative end-of-term termination-for-convenience right. The revision is not minimal because it additionally grants partial termination and uses a broad 'without ... further liability' waiver. That waiver, particularly when combined with 'notwithstanding anything to the contrary,' could impair accrued payment obligations, survival provisions, or other liabilities unrelated to the convenience termination, so unrelated commercial intent is not reliably preserved.
